streamHealth.title: Stream Performance
streamHealth.noData: No data has been collected yet. This page becomes available when a stream is live and has viewers.
streamHealth.intro1: This page is designed to help you find and isolate potential problems with your stream. Because it aggregates the experience of all viewers, a single viewer in an extremely poor situation can affect the overall numbers on a low-viewership stream.
streamHealth.intro2: This data is collected only from viewers using the AoiTube web viewing page. It does not reflect viewers watching in external players such as VLC, MPV, or QuickTime.
streamHealth.slowNetwork: Some viewers have a slow connection
streamHealth.bitrateError: At least one viewer is playing at {{speed}}kbps, which is slower than the lowest quality you offer ({{lowest}}kbps). If the errors continue, consider adding a lower-bitrate quality.
streamHealth.speedError: Viewers' playback may not be keeping up with the required speed. This can be caused by a slow connection or your latency settings. You need to reduce the time it takes viewers to consume the video. Try adding a lower-bitrate quality or increasing your latency buffer setting.

segmentSection.title: Segment Downloads
segmentSection.p1: If video segments take too long to download, viewers will experience buffering. When downloads are slow, possible remedies include offering a lower quality (lower bitrate) or improving delivery with external storage, a CDN, or a faster connection. For some viewers, increasing the latency buffer can also help.
segmentSection.p2: As a rule of thumb, if the pink line consistently approaches the blue line, viewers are likely experiencing problems.

networkSection.title: Viewer Network Speed
networkSection.p1: This is your viewers' playback bitrate (a rough indicator of their connection). When a viewer's bitrate falls below the bitrate of the lowest quality you offer, buffering becomes more likely. If you have viewers on slow connections, consider adding an even lower quality.
networkSection.p2: As a rule of thumb, if the pink line approaches the lowest blue line, at least one viewer may be experiencing problems.

errorsSection.title: Errors and Quality Changes
errorsSection.p1: These are the number of recent errors (such as buffering) and the number of quality changes across all viewers. Errors can be caused by many factors, such as browser issues, extensions, or a poor Wi-Fi connection. Not all of them are fatal or within your control as the streamer.
errorsSection.p2: Quality changes are not necessarily a bad thing, but if they happen frequently and errors are increasing at the same time, consider adding another quality variant.

latencySection.title: Viewer Latency
latencySection.description: This is a rough measure of how far behind the live video your viewers are (in seconds). The biggest cause of latency spikes is buffering. High latency is not itself a problem; over-optimizing for low latency can cause buffering, which can ultimately increase latency even further.

codecSelector.appliesNextStream: Changes to the video codec setting take effect the next time you start streaming.
codecSelector.descLibx264: libx264 is the default codec and is often effectively the only option in shared VPS environments. Unless you're sure you have another option enabled, we recommend using this one.
codecSelector.descNvenc: If you have a relatively recent NVIDIA GPU with encoding cores, you can encode on the GPU.
codecSelector.descVaapi: VA-API may be available with NVIDIA's proprietary drivers or with the Mesa drivers for AMD/Intel.
codecSelector.descQsv: Quick Sync is Intel's hardware for video encoding and decoding. It's an option if you have a relatively recent Intel CPU with an integrated GPU.
codecSelector.descV4l2: Video4Linux is an interface for accessing several hardware encoding backends, such as those for Intel and AMD.
codecSelector.descOmx: OpenMax is a codec used primarily on the Raspberry Pi.
codecSelector.descVideoToolbox: Apple VideoToolbox is a low-level framework for directly accessing hardware encoders and decoders.
codecSelector.title: Video codec

streamProtocol.iceServersArrayError: Please specify ICE servers as an array
streamProtocol.iceServersInvalid: The ICE server configuration is invalid
streamProtocol.latencySaveError: Failed to save the latency level
streamProtocol.title: Streaming Protocol Settings
streamProtocol.description: Configure the streaming protocol for your viewers. WebRTC delivers ultra-low latency (~1 second or less), while LL-HLS delivers low latency (~2-3 seconds).
streamProtocol.experimentalDescription: WebRTC and LL-HLS are experimental features. If you change these settings while streaming, a restart may be required.
streamProtocol.standardHlsDescription: Standard HLS streaming. The most compatible and stable option. Latency: ~10-30 seconds
streamProtocol.llhlsDescription: Apple LL-HLS protocol. Supported in Safari, iOS, and modern browsers. Latency: ~2-5 seconds
streamProtocol.maxViewersTip: 0 = unlimited. Set this according to your server resources.
streamProtocol.webrtcDescription: Real-time communication protocol. Delivers the lowest latency. Latency: ~0.5-2 seconds
streamProtocol.iceServersTip: Specify STUN/TURN servers as a JSON array. The urls field must be an array. If NAT traversal is required, configuring a TURN server is recommended.
streamProtocol.udpPortTip: The single UDP port all WebRTC media (ICE) is muxed onto. It must be opened inbound in your firewall. Changes take effect after a server restart (the port binds once at startup). The OWNCAST_WEBRTC_UDP_PORT environment variable overrides this value. Default: 52000.

external.title: External source (IVS / IVS-compatible)
external.gatingWarning: Note: external delivery cannot enforce the paywall (PPV / member-only / silent mode). Keep gated streams self-hosted.
external.description: Delegate delivery to a managed service (e.g. AWS IVS), an IVS-compatible service, or another node; viewers play its HLS URL directly. No local transcoding runs, saving CPU. Online status is derived by polling the URL.

offlineMessage.tip: An optional message to display to viewers when the stream is offline.

welcomeMessage.label: Welcome Message
welcomeMessage.tip: A system chat message sent to viewers when they first connect to chat. Leave blank to disable.

logo.label: Logo
logo.tip: The icon used across the whole site: header, favicon, notifications and the Fediverse profile image. A square JPG/PNG (e.g. 512×512 or larger) is recommended. Changes apply immediately; browser tab icons refresh on the next visit.

adminPassword.label: Admin Password
adminPassword.tip: Keep this password in a safe place. You will need it to log in to the admin dashboard!

ffmpegPath.label: FFmpeg Path
ffmpegPath.tip: The absolute file path to the FFMPEG application on your server

webPort.label: AoiTube Port
webPort.tip: The port the AoiTube web server listens on. Default is 8080

rtmpPort.label: RTMP Port
rtmpPort.tip: The port used to receive your stream. Default is 1935

instanceUrl.label: Server URL
instanceUrl.tip: The full URL of your AoiTube server.

socketHostOverride.label: Websocket Host Override
socketHostOverride.tip: The direct URL of your AoiTube server.

nsfw.label: Adult Content?
nsfw.tip: Turn this on if you plan to stream adult content. This ensures your stream is displayed correctly in the directory.

directoryEnabled.label: Enable Directory
directoryEnabled.tip: Turn this on to be listed in the directory.

hideViewerCount.label: Hide Viewer Count
hideViewerCount.tip: Turn this on to hide the viewer count on the web page.

silentStreamMode.label: Silent Mode (Test Stream)
silentStreamMode.tip: When enabled, no external notifications are sent when the stream starts, and the stream is visible only to admins and moderators (it is also not published to S3/CDN). The change takes effect from the next stream start.

chatDisable.label: Chat
chatDisable.tip: Turn the chat feature on your AoiTube server on or off.

chatJoinMessages.label: Join Messages
chatJoinMessages.tip: Show a message when a viewer joins the chat.

chatEstablishedUsers.label: Established Users Only
chatEstablishedUsers.tip: Only users who have been registered for a certain amount of time can chat.

chatSpamProtection.label: Spam Protection
chatSpamProtection.tip: Limits how quickly consecutive messages can be posted to prevent spam. Disabling this removes rate limiting.

chatSlurFilter.label: Slur Filter
chatSlurFilter.tip: Blocks messages that contain discriminatory or offensive words (mainly in English).

requireSocialAuth.label: Require Social Authentication
requireSocialAuth.tip: Requires X or Discord authentication to join the chat. Configure each service's API credentials in the notification settings beforehand.

forbiddenUsernames.label: Forbidden Usernames
forbiddenUsernames.tip: A list of words that are forbidden in chat usernames.

suggestedUsernames.label: Default Usernames
suggestedUsernames.tip: An optional list of chat usernames to assign to new users. If fewer than 10 are provided, random names are generated. Users can change their name later, and the same username may be assigned multiple times.
suggestedUsernames.minNotReached: This feature requires at least 10 entries.
suggestedUsernames.noEntries: The default name generator will be used.

federationEnabled.label: Enable Fediverse Features
federationEnabled.tip: Send and receive activity on the Fediverse.

federationPrivate.label: Private
federationPrivate.tip: Follow requests will require approval, and only followers will be able to see your activity.

federationShowEngagement.label: Show Engagement
federationShowEngagement.tip: Follows, likes, and shares will appear in the chat feed.

federationLiveMessage.placeholder: The stream has started! Come and watch!
federationLiveMessage.label: Go Live Message
federationLiveMessage.tip: A message announcing that your live stream has started. Tags are added automatically. Leave blank to disable.

federationDefaultUser.label: Username
federationDefaultUser.tip: The username used to send and receive activity on the Fediverse. For example, using "bob" will send messages from @bob@yourserver. Do not change this once you have followers.

federationInstanceUrl.label: Server URL
federationInstanceUrl.tip: The full URL of your AoiTube server is required to enable Fediverse features. It must use SSL (https). Do not change this once you have followers.

federationNsfw.label: Possibly Adult Content
federationNsfw.tip: Turn this on if you plan to stream adult content, so that previews of your stream can be marked as sensitive.

federationBlockedDomains.label: Blocked Domains
federationBlockedDomains.tip: You can block interactions from specific domains.

videoVariant.videoPassthroughTip: Enabling this disables all other settings. Leave it off and configure as usual.
videoVariant.audioPassthroughTip: If you select "No", set your desired audio bitrate.

name.label: Name
name.tip: A human-readable name to display in the player.

framerate.tip: Lowering the frame rate reduces the amount of video encoded and sent to viewers, saving CPU and bandwidth (at the cost of smoothness). A lower rate is fine for most content.

tooltips.fps24: 24fps - For movies, presentations, music, and low-spec or low-bandwidth servers.
tooltips.fps25: 25fps - For movies, presentations, music, and low-spec or low-bandwidth servers.
tooltips.fps30: 30fps - For slow or casual games, chatting, and general use.
tooltips.fps50: 50fps - For fast or action games, sports, and HD video.
tooltips.fps60: 60fps - For fast or action games, sports, and HD video.
tooltips.fps90: 90fps - For the latest fast-paced games and high-performance hardware.
tooltips.fps120: 120fps - Experimental. Use at your own risk.

videoBitrate.tip: The overall quality of your stream is generally affected most by the bitrate.

tooltips.level0: Lowest hardware usage - lowest quality video
tooltips.level1: Low hardware usage - low quality video
tooltips.level2: Medium hardware usage - average quality video
tooltips.level3: High hardware usage - high quality video
tooltips.level4: Highest hardware usage - higher quality video

encoderRecommendation.helpText: Only one video quality variant is configured. If your server has enough computing resources, consider adding another lower-quality variant so more people can watch your content!

servingEndpoint.label: Serving Endpoint
servingEndpoint.tip: Specify this if you want to serve content from a URL other than the default (used with CDNs and some storage providers). This is usually not needed.

forcePathStyle.label: Force Path Style
forcePathStyle.tip: Turn this on if your S3 provider does not support virtual-hosted-style URLs (e.g. Oracle Cloud Object Storage).

webhookUrl.tip: The Webhook assigned to your channel.

goLiveMessage.label: Go Live Text
goLiveMessage.tip: The text to send when your stream starts.
goLiveMessage.placeholder: The stream has started! Come and watch!

goLiveMessage.label: Go Live Text
goLiveMessage.tip: The text to send when your stream starts.
goLiveMessage.placeholder: The stream has started! Come and watch!

livePoster.label: Live poster
livePoster.tip: Shown in the player right after the stream starts (before the first thumbnail is generated) and before a viewer presses play. A 16:9 JPG/PNG (e.g. 1280×720 or larger) is recommended. The built-in "LIVE" image is used when unset. About 20 seconds into the broadcast it switches to the auto-generated thumbnail.

recordingEnabled.label: Record streams
recordingEnabled.tip: When enabled, streams are automatically saved as archives (VOD) after they end so viewers can watch them later. Changes take effect from the next stream.

recordingRetention.label: Recording retention
recordingRetention.tip: Maximum number of unpublished recordings to keep; the oldest are deleted automatically once exceeded. 0 means unlimited. Published, members-only, paid and ever-purchased archives are never auto-deleted.

recordingStoreS3.label: Store recordings on S3
recordingStoreS3.tip: When enabled, recording media is offloaded to S3 object storage (same bucket as live distribution, under archives/) after a stream ends, freeing local disk. Playback is proxied through the server so hidden-archive protection is preserved. Configure S3 credentials first under Server Settings > Storage.

backupEnabled.label: Enable automatic backups
backupEnabled.tip: When enabled, the database is backed up on a schedule.

backupInterval.label: Backup interval (hours)
backupInterval.tip: How often to run a backup, in hours. Minimum 1, default 24.

backupRetention.label: Local retention
backupRetention.tip: Maximum number of local backup files to keep; older ones are pruned automatically. 0 keeps all.

backupStoreS3.label: Store backups on S3
backupStoreS3.tip: Also upload each backup to S3 object storage (same bucket as live distribution, under backups/). Survives disk loss and eases node migration. Configure S3 credentials first.
